questions.stem: Q1. 4-year-old child was brought to the hospital with a history of loose stools. No history of fever or blood in stools. The mother says he is irritable and eagerly drinks water if given. On examination, eyes are sunken and in the skin pinch test, the skin retracted within two seconds but not immediately. What treatment is advised for the child?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. 4-year-old child was brought to the hospital with a history of loose stools. No history of fever or blood in stools. The mother says he is irritable and eagerly drinks water if given. On examination, eyes are sunken and in the skin pinch test, the skin retracted within two seconds but not immediately. What treatment is advised for the child?

options.label: A
options.text: Give oral fluids and zinc supplementation only and ask mother to come back if danger sign develops.

options.label: B
options.text: Give oral fluids and ask mother to continue the same and visit again the next day.

options.label: C
options.text: Consider severe dehydration start IV fluids, IV antibiotics, and refer to higher centre.

questions.stem: Q1. Which of the following is a true statement about congenital CMV infection?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. Which of the following is a true statement about congenital CMV infection?

options.label: A
options.text: About 20-30% of the infections are symptomatic

options.label: B
options.text: Triad of SNHL, periventricular calcification and enamel hypoplasia

options.label: C
options.text: Most children asymptomatic at birth can develop conductive hearing loss later in life

options.label: D
options.text: If mother is IgG positive for CMV, the child is unlikely to develop infection
